fields.summary: Planned change set Machine trust. The owner was asleep: an orchestrator answered as the owner's proxy under the owner's standing instruction to act on their behalf, so every pick below is the agent's option assumed for the owner, never the owner's words. Settled: the change set serves milestone-24. A machine's trust lives in a machine config file, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/machine.toml (default ~/.config), as trust = "dedicated" | "daily". It is set only by hand-editing that file: rhiza has no command or API operation that writes trust. A missing file means daily; a malformed file or unknown value is an error naming the file, and bypass stays refused. Trust changes no default permission mode, it only lifts the refusal of bypassPermissions. Trust shows in a read-only rhiza machine show and in a machine part of rhiza health. Trust is read live at every check (session start, session run, run start, daemon start), and no session record carries it. The orchestrator said the owner's intent tonight is that this VM is dedicated and every agent session on it runs in bypassPermissions: that is done on the VM by writing the machine config and setting rhiza.daemon.permissionMode=bypassPermissions after this lands, since no built-in workflow step sets its own mode. Nothing left open.
fields.title: Machine trust plan, with the orchestrator as the owner's proxy
